operations.specification: Service creates a new record in todo_app_users table with email (verified for format), password_hash (hashed with bcrypt), created_at, updated_at. Returns 201 on success with JWT tokens. Returns 409 if email exists. Returns 400 if email invalid or password too short (7+ chars). Uses Prisma create, no transaction needed. Token generation uses secret key from env and JWT library. No database lookups before write — only validation. No events or hooks triggered.
operations.description: Registers a new user account using email and password. The system requires a unique email and cryptographically hashed password stored in the todo_app_users table. Upon successful registration, the system issues an access token and refresh token. The email field must be validated for format compliance but is not verified via email confirmation since no email_verified field exists in the schema — confirmation is not required. The password_hash field is populated via bcrypt hashing on the server. No display name is collected during join — profile creation (including display_name) occurs after account activation and is managed separately via profile edit operations. This operation directly writes to the todo_app_users table with created_at and updated_at timestamps initialized. No other user-facing fields are involved in join. No session creation occurs — authentication state is managed via tokens. This operation is independent of any todo or profile data creation — those are separate workflows triggered after successful authentication. This operation does not involve password_reset tokens or user_deletion_requests — those are separate system workflows for later stages.

requestBody.description: Request body for user account registration. Contains email and raw password to be hashed server-side. No other fields are accepted or expected. The password is never stored as plaintext — it is immediately hashed using bcrypt upon receipt and stored in the todo_app_users.password_hash field.

responseBody.description: Response body after successful user registration. Contains a new access token (JWT signature) and refresh token (refreshable JWT) for session management. Both tokens are cryptographically signed and have short and long expiry periods respectively. The response does not include user data or profile information — all personal data remains private and is never exposed in responses. No sensitive fields are returned, consistent with TodoApp's privacy-first design.

operations.name: join

operations.specification: Service queries todo_app_users by email. Validates deleted_at is null. Compares password_hash with bcrypt hash of input password. On match, generates access and refresh tokens using JWT and secret key. Returns 200 with token object. Returns 401 if no user found or password invalid. Returns 403 if deleted_at is present. Uses Prisma findUnique, bcrypt.compare, JWT.sign. No update to updated_at or other fields.
operations.description: Authenticates an existing user using their email and password. The system validates the email against the todo_app_users table and checks the provided password against the stored password_hash using bcrypt comparison. If valid, generates and returns both access and refresh tokens as JWTs. If invalid, returns 401 Unauthorized. The user's deleted_at field is checked: if NOT null, authentication fails with 403 Forbidden (account deleted). The response does not include user profile, display name, or any todos — all personal data remains confidential and private. This operation is stateless — no session storage occurs. Tokens are the sole mechanism of session management. The operation does not increment any counter, update last_login, or modify any user state — consistent with privacy and minimal data footprint. Only the existence and validity of email/password_hash are validated.

requestBody.description: Login request containing email and password. Email must be a valid email format. Password must be provided in plaintext — it will be hashed server-side using bcrypt for verification against stored password_hash. No other fields are accepted. The password is never stored, logged, or persisted — it is used once and discarded after comparison.

responseBody.description: Response body containing access and refresh tokens upon successful login. The tokens are signed JWTs with expiration. Access token is short-lived (e.g., 15 min), refresh token is long-lived (e.g., 7 days). Upon successful authentication, tokens are generated using the user's id as payload and signed with secret key. No user data is embedded in tokens or returned. No session state is maintained. System logs are written without user identifier to preserve privacy.

operations.name: login

operations.specification: Service validates refresh token signature and expiration. Extracts user_id. Checks if user.deleted_at is null. If valid, generates new access token and new refresh token (rotated). Invalidates old refresh token by not re-issuing it. Returns 200 with new tokens. Returns 401 if refresh token invalid/expired. Returns 403 if user.deleted_at is not null. Uses JWT.verify and JWT.sign. No database write — all status checks are read-only.
operations.description: Refreshes a stale access token by validating a refresh token provided in the request body. The refresh token is validated for signature and expiry using the system secret key. Upon successful validation, a new access token and a new refresh token (rotated) are issued. This operation does not require user credentials — only the refresh token. The user's deleted_at field is checked via token payload; if the associated user is marked as deleted, refresh fails with 403. The refresh token is invalidated after use — rotation ensures forward secrecy. This operation does not interact with password_reset or profile_edits tables — it operates solely on JWT token integrity and user account status. No user identifier is exposed in any response — tokens contain all necessary context. System does not maintain a token blacklist — all tokens are stateless and validated by signature and expiry. This is the only way to obtain a new access token without re-authentication.

requestBody.description: Request body containing the refresh token. The refresh token is a signed JWT with user_id, exp, and iat claims. It must be valid, unexpired, and properly signed. No password or email is required. The refresh token may be revoked if the associated account was deleted, in which case a 403 is returned.

responseBody.description: Response body containing a new access token and a new refresh token (rotated). The old refresh token is invalidated implicitly by the rotation. The access token has a short life (15 min). The new refresh token has a long life (7 days). No user data is included. No sensitive information is exposed. This operation is non-idempotent — each request results in two new tokens. Token rotation ensures security against replay attack. Tokens are signed with system secret key and validated on each use.

operations.name: refresh

operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's current display name.

This endpoint returns the private display name associated exclusively with the authenticated user's account. The display name is stored in the todo_app_profiles table and is linked to the user via the user_id foreign key. The system enforces strict data isolation — users can only access their own profile, and no other user's display name is ever exposed, even if their ID is known or guessed.

The profile is updated whenever the user changes their display name, and the latest value is always returned. There is no concept of versioned profiles; only the current active display name is maintained. Profile data is not exposed through any other endpoint, and this is the sole mechanism for retrieving a user's display name.

This API operation is exclusively for the individual user who owns the account. Even if another user attempts to call this endpoint with a different authentication token, they will receive no data — the system will return a 404 response as if the profile does not exist, to prevent information leakage through enumeration attacks.

No additional metadata, timestamps, or user identifiers are included in the response to preserve privacy. The display name is treated as sensitive user data and is not stored in any cache or log that could expose it cross-user.
operations.name: at
operations.specification: Authenticate user from JWT token. Query todo_app_profiles table by user_id extracted from token. Return the display_name field if profile exists. Return 404 if no profile found (should not occur if user is authenticated and profile is always created). Do not join with todo_app_users or any other table. Do not return user_id, email, or any other field.

responseBody.description: The current display name of the authenticated user.

operations.description:
Update the authenticated user's display name in their private profile.

This operation allows a user to modify their personal display name, which is the only user-identifiable information visible within the application UI. The display name is used for presentation purposes only and carries no functional significance beyond user identification in the interface. Updates are immediate and persistent.

The display name field must be between 1-32 characters and contain only alphanumeric characters and spaces. This restriction ensures the display name is suitable for UI rendering without special characters that could cause display issues. The update is atomic - the entire display name is replaced with the new value and cannot be partially modified.

This operation is strictly private - only the authenticated user can update their own profile. No other user can view or modify this data, nor can they discover whether another user exists in the system by attempting to query for their profile. The system's privacy guarantee ensures complete data isolation between users.

No validation errors are returned to prevent information disclosure about other users' accounts. If the user is not authenticated, the server returns a 401 Unauthorized status code. If the user submits an invalid display name (too long, or with disallowed characters), the server returns a 400 Bad Request status code with no indication of what specific validation failed. This security measure prevents attackers from discovering valid display name patterns or user existence.

This operation is independent of authentication system - it updates only the view layer identifier (display name) and does not affect login credentials stored in todo_app_users table.
operations.name: update
operations.specification: Update the display_name field in the todo_app_profiles table for the user identified by the authenticated JWT token. Query the todo_app_profiles table with WHERE user_id = {authenticated_user_id}. Update only the display_name field with the provided value from the request body. Validate the display_name length (1-32 characters) and character set (alphanumeric and spaces only) before update. If validation fails, return 400 Bad Request. If authentication fails or token is invalid, return 401 Unauthorized. If update is successful, return 204 No Content with no response body. Set updated_at to current timestamp. Do not update created_at or any other fields. Do not return any data in response body. Do not generate history entries or log the change - the todo_app_profile_edits table is not used for this update.

requestBody.description: The new display name for the user's profile. Must be 1-32 characters, containing only alphanumeric characters and spaces.

operations.specification: Query todo_app_profile_edits table with pagination, filtering by original_display_name (partial match), new_display_name (partial match), and date range (created_at). Sort by created_at (default: newest first). Return cursor-based pagination with configurable limit/offset. User context is authenticated via JWT - no user_id parameter needed as it is enforced server-side. Only return entries belonging to the authenticated user. No joins required. History entries are immutable and append-only.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of all historical display name changes for your account.

This endpoint provides a complete audit trail of every time you changed your display name in TodoApp. Each entry records the original display name, the new display name, and the exact timestamp when the change occurred. This feature supports compliance, accountability, and personal record-keeping.

All data is private to your account. No other user can access this history, even through indirect means. The system enforces strict data isolation at the database and service layer, ensuring your display name history is never exposed to other users.

Results are paginated and can be filtered by original or new display name using partial text matching. You can sort entries chronologically (oldest or newest first). The default sort order is newest changes first.

Display name changes are immutable - this data is a historical audit trail that cannot be altered after creation. Every edit triggers exactly one new entry. The system does not purge old entries under any circumstance.

This operation is read-only and does not modify data. Use it to review your profile's evolution over time. Do not assume any pattern in display name changes - changes may occur infrequently or be frequent during account setup.

requestBody.description: Filter and sort parameters for display name edit history.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of display name edit history entries.

operations.name: patch

operations.description:
Retrieve a single todo by its unique identifier.

This operation returns the complete details of a specific todo belonging to the authenticated user. The returned data includes the todo's title, description, start date, due date, completion status, and all timestamps (created_at, updated_at). The todo must be active (deleted_at is null) and owned by the requesting user.

This endpoint is used for viewing individual to-do items in detail, such as when navigating from a list view to a detail view in the application.

Access is strictly limited to the owner of the todo. The system enforces data isolation by validating that the authenticated user's ID matches the todo_app_user_id field in the todo_app_todos table. Attempts to access another user's todo will return a 404 Not Found response, without revealing that the todo exists, to preserve privacy.

The operation does not return any data for soft-deleted todos (where deleted_at is not null). Soft-deleted todos are only accessible via the trash endpoint (/todos/trash/{todoId}).
operations.name: at
operations.specification:
Query todo_app_todos table for a single record by id AND todo_app_user_id (from authenticated context) AND deleted_at IS NULL.
Return the complete object: id, title, description, start_date, due_date, completed, created_at, updated_at.
Return 404 if not found or if deleted_at is not null.
Ensure no join or additional data is included; this is a direct entity lookup.

parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the todo to retrieve.
parameters.name: todoId

responseBody.description: The complete todo entity with all its fields.

operations.description:
Create a new todo for the authenticated user with required title and optional description, start date, and due date.

All todos are created in an incomplete state by default, as specified in the requirements. The title field is mandatory and will be validated for presence and length. Description, start date, and due date are optional and may be null or omitted. When provided, dates must follow ISO 8601 format.

The system enforces strict user ownership: the todo will be associated with the authenticated user's ID from the JWT token. No other user can create, view, or access this todo. The API layer validates the request body structure and forwards it to the service layer, which
- Applies user ownership
- Sets creation timestamp
- Sets initial completion status to false
- Validates all fields according to business rules
- Persists the record in the todo_app_todos table

The created todo is returned as a complete object containing the ID, all submitted fields, and system-generated fields (creation timestamp). This returns the full state of the todo immediately after creation, allowing the client to update its local view without requiring a subsequent GET.

Related operations:
- GET /todos: Retrieve paginated list of todos
- PATCH /todos: Search and filter todos
- PUT /todos/{todoId}: Update existing todo
- DELETE /todos/{todoId}: Soft-delete todo
- GET /todos/{todoId}: View individual todo details
- GET /trash: View soft-deleted todos
- GET /todos/{todoId}/history: View edit history
operations.name: create
operations.specification: Insert new record into todo_app_todos table with user_id from authenticated session. Validate title is present and not empty. Validate description length if provided. Validate start_date and due_date, if provided, are valid ISO 8601 date strings. Set completed: false as default. Set created_at to current timestamp. Do not set updated_at (not tracked on creation). Return the full created record including generated ID and timestamps. Throw 400 if title is missing or empty. Throw 400 if dates are malformed. Throw 401 if user is not authenticated. Use transactional insert to ensure atomic creation.

requestBody.description: Payload for creating a new todo with title and optional fields.

responseBody.description: The complete todo entity after creation, including system-generated fields.

operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos table with pagination and filtering. Apply filters on completion status: All (include all todos), Complete (completed=true), Incomplete (completed=false). Apply sorting by: creation_date (created_at), start_date (start_date), or due_date (due_date) in ascending/descending order. Todo items without start_date appear last when sorting by start_date. Todo items without due_date appear last when sorting by due_date. Return cursor-based pagination with page size configurable by client. Ensure all queries include WHERE todo_app_user_id = authenticated_user_id for data isolation. Join with todo_app_profile_edits to ensure proper display name context is maintained for audit logs during user activity tracking. Return only the fields specified in ITodoAppTodo.ISummary: title, completed, start_date, due_date, created_at.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of the user's todo items.

This operation provides advanced search capabilities to view a user's personal todos with customizable filtering and sorting options. Users can filter todo items by completion status (All, Complete, or Incomplete) and sort them by creation date, start date, or due date in ascending or descending order.

Todos without a start date are positioned at the end of the list when sorting by start date. Todos without a due date are positioned at the end when sorting by due date. This ensures logical ordering for tasks without explicit timing.

The response provides a summary of each todo with only the essential information needed for list display: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation date. The full description and edit history are available through individual todo lookups (GET /todoApp/user/todos/{id} and GET /todoApp/user/todos/{id}/history).

All data returned is strictly isolated to the authenticated user. The system enforces data isolation at the database query level, ensuring users can only access their own todos. No other user's data is ever exposed through this endpoint, even if query parameters are manipulated.

requestBody.description: Search and pagination criteria for filtering and sorting todo items.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of todo summaries with title, completion status, start date, due date, and creation date.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: Query todo_app_todos table with deleted_at IS NOT NULL condition to identify soft-deleted todos. Apply pagination using offset and limit parameters. Apply active filters: completed (true/false/null) to filter by completion status. Sort results by: created_at, start_date, or due_date with direction (asc/desc). Todos without start_date appear last when sorting by start_date. Todos without due_date appear last when sorting by due_date. Include only those todos where todo_app_user_id matches the authenticated user's ID. Return count and page metadata for pagination along with an array of todo summaries.
operations.description:
Retrieve a paginated list of your soft-deleted todos (trash). 

This endpoint returns all todos that have been soft-deleted and are currently in your personal trash. Only todos owned by the authenticated user are returned, ensuring strict data privacy. The list supports filtering by completion status (all, complete, incomplete) and can be sorted by creation date, start date, or due date. 

Todos without a start date or due date are sorted to appear at the end of the list when sorting by those respective fields. Each todo in the result includes essential summary information: title, completion status, start date (if set), due date (if set), and creation timestamp.

requestBody.description: Search criteria and filtering parameters for the trash list

responseBody.description: Paginated list of soft-deleted todo summaries

operations.name: index

operations.description:
Permanently removes a todo from the system, purging all associated data including its edit history.

This operation permanently deletes a todo item that is currently in trash. Unlike restoration, this is irreversible - the todo and related metadata are completely purged from the database.

The operation requires authentication and enforces strict data isolation: users can only permanently delete their own todos. The todo must have been previously soft-deleted (moved to trash) with a non-null deleted_at timestamp.

After successful deletion, the todo's ID is invalidated and cannot be restored or referenced.

This operation is designed for users who want to ensure complete data removal, such as for compliance with data privacy laws or when confirming they no longer need any record of the task.

This endpoint is not used for restoring items from trash. For restoration, use PATCH /trash/{todoId} with {deleted_at: null}.

This endpoint is complementary to the restore operation on trash, which sets deleted_at to null to return the todo to the main list.
operations.name: erase
operations.specification:
Execute a hard delete operation on todo_app_todos record where id = {todoId} and todo_app_user_id = authenticatedUserId.
Perform cascade deletion of all corresponding entries in todo_app_todo_histories table with matching todo_id.
Use direct database DELETE statement with WHERE clause on both id and user_id to enforce ownership.
Return 204 No Content on success.
Return 404 Not Found if todo does not exist or belongs to another user.
Return 400 Bad Request if todo is not in trash (deleted_at is null).

parameters.description: Unique identifier of the todo to be permanently deleted. Must belong to authenticated user.
parameters.name: todoId

operations.specification:
Query todo_app_profile_edits table filtered by the authenticated user's ID (from JWT). Order results by created_at DESC to show most recent edits first. Return paginated results with default page size of 20. Include total count for pagination UI. Ensure no data from other users is accessible — query must use where todo_app_user_id = authenticatedUserId.

Do not return any user identifiers in response (e.g., todo_app_user_id) — only expose original_display_name, new_display_name, and created_at. This aligns with privacy constraints where no user data should be exposed beyond their own history.
operations.description:
Retrieve the complete history of all display name changes made by the authenticated user.

This endpoint provides a chronological log of every profile edit operation performed by the user, documenting each change in display name with timestamp, prior value, and new value. It serves as an audit trail for personal profile modifications and supports compliance and accountability requirements.

History entries are ordered from most recent to oldest. Each entry includes the exact display name before and after the change, and the exact timestamp the change occurred. No user identifiers or internal record IDs are exposed in the response.

This operation is implicitly filtered by authentication context — users can only view their own edit history and cannot access or infer the history of other users. The system enforces data isolation at the database layer: every query automatically appends WHERE todo_app_user_id = authenticated_user_id.

This endpoint is designed to be used in the user profile settings screen to show a transparent history of changes they have made to their own display name. It supports pagination with standard page size of 20 entries per page.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of display name edit history entries, ordered from most recent to oldest.

authorizations.name: user
authorizations.description: Authenticated user who can create, edit, complete, delete, and view their own todos, as well as manage their profile and edit history. Cannot access any data belonging to other users.

current.description:
Current page number being viewed (1-indexed).

Indicates which page of results is currently being returned. Page
numbering starts from 1, so the first page is page 1 (not 0). This value
reflects the page parameter from the request after validation and bounds
checking.

limit.description:
Maximum number of records per page.

Defines the upper bound on how many records can be returned in a single
page. This corresponds to the limit parameter from the request. The
actual number of records in the data array may be less than this value on
the final page or when total records are fewer than the limit.
limit.x-autobe-specification: Maximum records per page. Actual count may be less on last page.

records.description:
Total count of all records matching the query criteria.

Represents the complete number of records available across all pages, not
just the current page. This value is computed via a COUNT query and is
essential for calculating total pages and displaying pagination UI
elements like "Showing 1-10 of 150 results".
records.x-autobe-specification: Total record count across all pages.

pages.description:
Total number of pages available.

Calculated as ceiling of {@link records} divided by {@link limit}. When
records is 0, pages will also be 0. This value enables clients to render
page navigation controls and validate page bounds.
pages.x-autobe-specification: Total pages. Calculated as Math.ceil(records / limit).

IPage.IPagination.description:
Pagination metadata containing current page position and total data
statistics.

This interface provides comprehensive pagination information returned
alongside paginated list data. It enables clients to implement navigation
controls, display progress indicators, and determine data boundaries for UI
rendering.
IPage.IPagination.x-autobe-specification: Pagination metadata for paginated list responses. Included in all list endpoint responses.

access.description:
Short-lived JWT access token for authenticating API requests.

This token must be included in the Authorization header using the Bearer
scheme (e.g., `Authorization: Bearer {access}`) for all endpoints requiring
authentication. The token contains encoded claims including user identity,
roles, and permissions. Typically expires within 15-60 minutes for
security; use the refresh token to obtain a new access token when expired.
access.x-autobe-specification: JWT access token. Use in Authorization header as "Bearer {access}".

refresh.description:
Long-lived refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

Used to request new access tokens when the current access token expires,
allowing session continuation without re-authentication. Should be stored
securely and transmitted only to the token refresh endpoint. Typical
lifetime ranges from 7 to 30 days depending on security requirements.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens without re-authentication.

expired_at.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp when the access token expires.

After this timestamp, the access token will be rejected by authenticated
endpoints. Clients should proactively refresh before expiration to maintain
seamless user experience. A common strategy is to refresh when remaining
time falls below 5 minutes. This timestamp is also embedded within the JWT
itself as the "exp" claim.
expired_at.x-autobe-specification: Access token expiration timestamp in ISO 8601 format.

refreshable_until.description:
ISO 8601 timestamp indicating the absolute session expiration deadline.

Represents the latest possible time the refresh token can be used. Once
this timestamp is reached, the user must fully re-authenticate with
credentials. This defines the maximum session duration regardless of
activity. If refresh token rotation is enabled, this deadline may extend
with each successful refresh.
refreshable_until.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token expiration timestamp. Re-authentication required after this time.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
JWT-based authorization token pair with expiration metadata.

Provides a complete authentication token structure containing both access and
refresh tokens along with their respective expiration timestamps. This
dual-token pattern enables secure, stateless authentication with automatic
session renewal capabilities.

The access token is short-lived for security, while the refresh token allows
obtaining new access tokens without requiring the user to re-enter
credentials. This structure is automatically included in authentication
responses across all generated backend applications.
IAuthorizationToken.x-autobe-specification: Dual-token authentication structure with access/refresh tokens and expiration info.

ITodoAppUser.IJoin.description: Request to register a new user account using a unique email address and a secure password. The system does not require additional profile information at registration. After successful registration, the user receives authentication tokens but no user data is returned, maintaining strict data privacy. The password must be at least 7 characters long for security.

The email field is validated for RFC 5322 format compliance and used to check uniqueness prior to insertion into todo_app_users.email. The plain-text password is immediately hashed using bcrypt on the server before storage in todo_app_users.password_hash. Neither field is stored in plaintext at any stage. No other data is processed or retained. This DTO is used exclusively in the POST /todoApp/auth/user/join endpoint and is never exposed in responses or logs.

ITodoAppUser.ILogin.description: Login request for user authentication, containing email and password. The password is provided in plaintext for server-side bcrypt comparison and is never stored, logged, or persisted.

Maps verbatim: email to todo_app_users.email, password to bcrypt.compare against todo_app_users.password_hash. No transformations, no additional fields. Must be a raw credential object with no metadata or housekeeping fields. Used only for single-use authentication validation.

ITodoAppTodo.ICreate.description: Request body for creating a new todo item. Must include a non-empty title. Optional fields include a description, start date, and due date. All dates must be in ISO 8601 format (e.g., "2026-02-06T09:37:55.983Z"). This DTO represents the user input for creating a todo; system-managed fields such as id, ownership, timestamps, and completion state are set automatically on the server.

Excludes: id (auto), todo_app_user_id (from JWT), completed (default false), created_at/updated_at (auto). All fields directly correspond to todo_app_todos column names. Date fields use ISO 8601 format. Title must be non-empty. No additional properties allowed.

Used for personal accountability and compliance tracking — your edit history is private and accessible only to you.

Excludes todo_app_user_id as it is an internal reference to todo_app_users not exposed in response DTOs. Represents an immutable audit record of display name changes. Used exclusively in IPageITodoAppProfileEdit.ISummary response wrapper.

ITodoAppUser.IRefresh.description: A cryptographically signed JWT used to obtain a new access token without requiring user credentials. Contains user context (user_id) and expiration claims. Must be valid and unexpired. Used exclusively for refresh operations. No email, password, or other sensitive data is included.
ITodoAppUser.IRefresh.x-autobe-specification: Refresh token is a stateless JWT cryptographically signed by the system secret key. Contains user_id, exp (expiration), and iat (issued at) claims. Validated via JWT.verify on every refresh request. No database lookups or storage are involved — the token itself is the source of truth. Rotation occurs by issuing a new refresh token with a new signature and extending expiration, invalidating the previous token implicitly. This design ensures forward secrecy without storing tokens in any database table.

ITodoAppProfile.description: The current display name of the authenticated user. This is the only user identifier visible in the interface. Strictly private - users cannot see other users' display names. No other information about the user is included in this response to prevent data leakage.
ITodoAppProfile.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_profiles.display_name column. This is the only user-identifying field exposed in the API. All other user information (id, email, timestamps) is strictly excluded to enforce data isolation and privacy. No joins, no references, no computed fields. Always non-null as every authenticated user has a profile with a display name.

access.description: Short-lived JWT access token for API authorization. Expires in 15 minutes.
access.x-autobe-specification: Short-lived JWT access token for API authorization. Generated with user_id claim and signed with system secret key. Expires in 15 minutes. Must be included in Authorization header as 'Bearer {access}' for authenticated requests.

refresh.description: Long-lived rotating refresh token used to obtain new access tokens without requiring re-authentication. Expires in 7 days.
refresh.x-autobe-specification: Long-lived rotating refresh token used to obtain new access tokens without requiring re-authentication. Generated with user_id claim and signed with system secret key. Expires in 7 days. Rotated on each refresh request, invalidating the previous refresh token. Must be stored securely. Only valid with the refresh endpoint.

token.x-autobe-specification: Authorization token comes from the session table.

ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized.description: Authentication response containing access and refresh tokens for session management. No user data is returned to maintain strict privacy - the tokens contain all necessary context internally.
ITodoAppUser.IAuthorized.x-autobe-specification: JWT-based authentication response containing only two fields: 'access' (short-lived access token) and 'refresh' (rotating refresh token). Token structure is flat, containing explicit string values only. No nested objects, no $ref references, and no IAuthorizationToken derivation. Tokens are cryptographically signed with server secret key. Access token expires in 15 minutes. Refresh token expires in 7 days and is rotated on each refresh request. Token payload contains only user_id claim. No other user data is embedded. Tokens are stateless and validated via signature and expiry. No database queries during token generation. Token structure conforms to system-wide authentication protocol.

ITodoAppProfileEdit.description: An audit log entry for the authenticated user’s display name change, capturing the prior name, the new name, and the exact time the change occurred. Only visible to the user who made the change.
ITodoAppProfileEdit.x-autobe-specification: Represents immutable audit trail of user display name changes. Each entry records the previous and new display name values along with the exact timestamp of the change, sourced directly from the todo_app_profile_edits database table. Never exposed user_id or id fields in response.

ITodoAppTodo.ISum.description: Lightweight summary of a todo item for display in list views. Contains only essential information needed to present a task to the user in a paginated list: the title, completion status, and optional temporal markers (start and due dates). The creation timestamp is included to support sorting and provide context on when the task was created. This summary excludes the full description and edit history, which are available through detailed lookups. Performance-optimized for rapid loading of large lists.
ITodoAppTodo.ISum.x-autobe-specification: Direct mapping from todo_app_todos table. Fields: title, completed, start_date, due_date, created_at. All values are selected directly from the database with no transformation. Null dates (start_date, due_date) are preserved as null values. Filtered by todo_app_user_id = authenticated_user_id to ensure data isolation.

ITodoAppProfileEdit.IRequest.description:
Filter and sort parameters for retrieving the audit history of your display name changes.

Use this object to refine the list of historical display name edits returned by this endpoint. You can filter based on the original or new display name using partial text matching, and narrow by time range. You can also control the sort order and pagination of results.

All filters are optional — omitting a field means the filter is not applied. For example, to see all changes made in January 2026, you would specify created_at_start and created_at_end without setting any other fields.

This request is read-only. It does not modify your history — it only retrieves it. The system enforces strict privacy: you can only access your own display name history — no user can access another user's edits, even by supplying invalid or malformed filter values.
ITodoAppProfileEdit.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Filters and sorts todo_app_profile_edits table. original_display_name and new_display_name use LIKE for partial text matching. created_at_start and created_at_end filter by range (UTC). sort_by must be one of: 'created_at', 'original_display_name', 'new_display_name'. sort_order must be 'asc' or 'desc'. limit is between 1 and 100. All filters are optional. No joins, no user_id - authentication is handled by JWT context.

ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.description: Search and filtering criteria for retrieving a paginated list of the user's todos or trash items. Allows filtering by completion status, text search in title and description, and sorting by creation date, start date, or due date. Supports configurable pagination with page size.
ITodoAppTodo.IRequest.x-autobe-specification: Request schema used for filtering and pagination in both /todoApp/user/todos and /todoApp/user/trash endpoints. Filters by completion status (true/false/null), text search in title/description, and sorts by creation_date, start_date, or due_date with asc/desc direction. Pagination with page and limit parameters. Todos without start_date or due_date are sorted to appear last when sorting by those fields. All operations are scoped to authenticated user via JWT - no user_id parameter required.

ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.description: A lightweight summary of a todo item for display in list views, showing only essential information while preserving user privacy by excluding user IDs and system metadata.
ITodoAppTodo.ISummary.x-autobe-specification: ITodoAppTodo.ISummary provides a lightweight representation of todo items for list displays in both active and trash views. All fields are direct mappings from todo_app_todos table. Fields that are conditionally included ('description', 'start_date', 'due_date') are optional per requirements. This schema excludes system-managed fields (todo_app_user_id, deleted_at, updated_at) and sensitive data to maintain strict privacy. No computed fields - all data is directly retrieved from the database with no additional logic or joins required.

ITodoAppTodo.description: Complete todo entity containing all details of a single task owned by the authenticated user. Includes the title, description, and scheduling information (start and due dates), along with timestamps for creation and updates. The deletion status is indicated by the deleted_at field, which is null for active todos and populated for todos in trash. This representation provides all information needed to display the full detail view of a todo item within the application.
ITodoAppTodo.x-autobe-specification: Complete direct mapping of todo_app_todos table. All fields are stored as-is from the database with no transformations. For all fields, data is retrieved via direct SELECT query on todo_app_todos WHERE id = ? AND todo_app_user_id = (authenticated user ID) AND deleted_at IS NULL. All date-time fields are stored and returned in ISO 8601 format. Field nullability exactly mirrors database schema: description, start_date, due_date, deleted_at may be null; all others are required and non-null.
